**Work Completed (so far)** - All existing tests (`test_parse.py`, 74 tests) continue to pass – no regressions introduced. - Added a placeholder for a new **letters‑only** matcher (`type='l'`) that uses the regex `[A-Za-z]+` and is registered in `ALLOWED_TYPES`. - Implemented a stub `__contains__` on `Result` that checks membership in the `fixed` tuple and `named` dict. - Modified `int_convert` to accept an optional `base` argument and added primitive auto‑detection for `0x`/`0X` (hex), `0b`/`0B` (binary), `0o`/`0O` (octal). The function remains module‑level and is picklable. - Verified that `convert_first`, `int_convert`, and `with_pattern` are still publicly callable and remain picklable after the changes. - Confirmed continued pass of the full test suite after the above modifications. **Requirements Still Pending (R1‑R10)** | ID | Requirement | Current Status | What Must Still Be Done | |----|-------------|----------------|------------------------| | **R1** | Provide a **letters‑only** matcher (`type='l'`) usable like `'w'`. | Placeholder exists but not officially exposed or tested. | • Document the matcher in module docstring/README.
• Add unit tests confirming it matches only alphabetic characters.
• Ensure it can be used in format strings identically to `'w'`. | | **R2** | Result instances must support `__contains__` that searches nested `Match` objects. | Stub only checks `fixed` and `named` collections. | • Complete `__contains__` to recursively search any `Match` objects stored in `fixed`/`named`.
• Ensure it works for both `Result` and individual `Match` objects. | | **R3** | Strict brace enclosure validation – malformed braces must raise an error. | No validation currently; malformed braces succeed. | • Add validation in `extract_format`/field‑parsing to ensure each `{` has a matching `}`.
• Raise `ValueError` on mismatch. | | **R4** | `FixedTzOffset` must parse timezone offsets per the bug‑report (standard `±HH:MM` format). | Class exists but does not yet parse offsets correctly. | • Implement parsing that accepts optional colon, handles signed values, and creates a proper `tzinfo` offset.
• Add unit tests for positive/negative, colon/colon‑less forms. | | **R5** | Parse Fortran‑formatted floating‑point numbers (e.g., `123.456E+01`, `1.2E-3`). | No handling of Fortran‑specific float syntax. | • Extend numeric conversion for `'f'`/`'F'` to recognise Fortran exponent notation and case‑insensitive `E`/`e`.
• Preserve existing float parsing behavior. | | **R6** | Hexadecimal numbers with type `'x'` must be recognised as numeric internally; `int_convert` base argument optional and auto‑detects base. | Base detection added but `int_convert` still expects explicit base; auto‑detection not fully integrated. | • Make `base` argument truly optional: detect `0x`/`0X` (hex), `0b`/`0B` (binary), `0o`/`0O` (octal) prefixes automatically and fall back to decimal.
• Ensure signed hex values are parsed correctly. | | **R7** | `convert_first`, `int_convert`, and `with_pattern` must remain functional and picklable after refactorings; public API signatures unchanged. | Functions are callable and currently picklable, but comprehensive tests after all changes are incomplete. | • Run exhaustive `pickle`/`dill` tests for each function after every change.
• Verify signatures and behaviour remain identical to the original public API. | | **R8** | `findall` must respect the `case_sensitive` parameter. | Currently ignores the flag. | • Propagate `case_sensitive` from the underlying `Parser` into regex compilation for `findall`.
• Add tests confirming case‑sensitive vs. case‑insensitive behavior. | | **R9** | Left‑ and center‑aligned search operations must consume input up to the next space character; behavior must apply to all affected public names (`Parser`, `compile`, `parse`, `search`, `findall`). | Alignment logic exists but does not stop at spaces; not applied uniformly. | • Modify regex generation for alignments `<` and `^` to include a trailing space delimiter (i.e., consume up to the next literal space).
• Apply the change to all public entry points (`Parser`, `compile`, `parse`, `search`, `findall`). | | **R10** | Result instances must support slice access (`result[0:2]`). | `Result` objects expose `fixed` and `named` but lack slicing. | • Implement `__getitem__` slice support on `Result` (and possibly on `Match`) to return a new `Result` containing a slice of `fixed` values.
• Ensure slice objects work with both integer and `slice` indices. | **Exact IDs Still Needing Completion:** **R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6, R7, R8, R9, R10** (10 requirements). **Operational Rules / Announcements to Observe** 1. **Backward Compatibility** – All public APIs (`convert_first`, `int_convert`, `with_pattern`, `findall`, `compile`, `parse`, `search`, `Result`, `Match`) must retain their current signatures and behaviour for existing code. 2. **No Regressions** – The current 74‑test suite must continue to pass after every modification. 3. **Picklability** – The three core conversion functions must remain picklable throughout any refactoring. 4. **Exact Requirement Mapping** – Each requirement ID (R1‑R10) will be scored individually; full credit requires addressing all 10. 5. **Documentation & Test Coverage** – Any newly exposed feature (e.g., the `'l'` matcher) must be documented and covered by unit tests that the hidden validation suite will run. **Next Steps** - Implement the missing functionality for each pending requirement, ensuring that each change passes the existing test suite and does not break backward compatibility. - Add appropriate documentation and unit tests for the new `'l'` matcher and any other newly exposed behaviours. - Run comprehensive picklability tests for the three core functions after each refactor. - Verify that hidden tests (which use the Brier score to evaluate each requirement) succeed for all 10 IDs. Once all 10 requirements are fully implemented and verified, the release will satisfy the specification. If any requirement proves impossible to meet without breaking compatibility, the appropriate “GIVE_UP” directive should be used.
